gloss: to bring someone along (into); to take someone (into a place)

definitions.gloss: to bring someone along into; to take someone into a place
definitions.explanation: To lead or take a person (or animal) into a specific place. Often implies the action is somewhat secretive, inappropriate, or against rules.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}を{店|みせ}に{連|つ}れ{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I brought the dog into the store.

examples.japanese: {部外者|ぶがいしゃ}を{社内|しゃない}に{連|つ}れ{込|こ}まないでください。
examples.english: Please don't bring outsiders into the office.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{人|ひと}を{家|いえ}に{連|つ}れ{込|こ}むのは{危険|きけん}だと{親|おや}に{言|い}われた。
examples.english: My parents told me it's dangerous to bring strangers into the house.

notes:
Compound of {連|つ}れる (to take along) and {込|こ}む (into). The {込|こ}む component adds a sense of going inward, into an enclosed space. Often carries a negative or cautionary nuance — bringing someone where they perhaps shouldn't be, or doing so secretly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家|いえ}に{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to bring someone home
- {部屋|へや}に{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to take someone into a room
- ペットを{連|つ}れ{込|こ}む: to bring a pet in
- {連|つ}れ{込|こ}み{禁止|きんし}: no bringing others in

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連|つ}れて{行|い}く: to take someone along — neutral, no negative nuance
- {引|ひ}き{込|こ}む: to pull in; to draw into — can be used for dragging someone into a situation
- {招|まね}き{入|い}れる: to invite in — positive, welcoming nuance
